engine.title: The multibagger screen qualified nobody for four weeks
engine.body: Corrects what this entry said on 2026-08-27. It read ‘the scan is running on schedule’ and blamed the fixed list on cadence. The ledger says otherwise: the last multibagger row is 2026-08-01, while magic, magicmagic and ai_longterm — the same Saturday job, the same slot — all logged 2026-08-22. Twenty-six days, three Saturdays, nothing written.
engine.note: The screen is not broken. Run on 2026-08-27 it took 11 candidates and rejected 10 for R:R below 2.0 — CHENNPETRO 1.29, FLUOROCHEM 1.07, GLAXO 0.59, which needs a 63% win rate merely to break even. The defect was that a week qualifying nobody wrote nothing at all, so the page served the 1 August list as though it were current. The attempt is recorded either way now. The gate is NOT loosened: publishing a 0.59 R:R to keep the section busy is the exact trade this screen exists to refuse, and an empty week is a real result.

engine.title: Stop buying strength that has already run
engine.body: The 4H RSI ceiling for longs was 75. Splitting every closed trade by the RSI recorded at entry showed the engine bleeding above 65 and profitable below it. The ceiling is now 65.
engine.note: Holds in both halves of the sample and at every cut point tested (60, 65, 70), so it is not one lucky threshold. The threshold was still chosen from this sample, so treat the size as an upper bound.

engine.title: A break-even stop would not have helped
engine.body: The median losing trade was +1.44R in profit before it reversed, and 59% touched a full +1R first. That looks like an obvious fix: move the stop to entry once price pays 1R. Re-walking every trade bar by bar, with winners subject to the same rule, says otherwise.
engine.note: The first version of this test only altered losers, which guarantees a positive answer. Correcting it reversed the conclusion. Nothing tested cleared one standard error, so no stop rule was adopted.

engine.title: Trades were being closed at prices that never traded
engine.body: The grader had never resolved a single trade — an exception was being swallowed silently — leaving a fallback path that could book an exit at a bar from before the signal existed. Every closed trade was re-graded against bars that actually printed.
evidence: exits corrected to a real price
engine.note: This moved the headline number against me. It is published anyway, because the earlier number was not real. Pre-correction data is kept in the repo rather than deleted.

engine.title: A first target must pay back the risk
engine.body: T1 was whichever structural level sat nearest the entry, with no distance test. One signal shipped a T1 worth 0.19R against its own stop, printed beside an R:R of 2.41 quoted off T2. T1 must now return at least 1R.

chess.title: Endgame: King Activity

Rule: when queens are off the board, march your king to the centre. Opposition matters: two kings facing each other, one move apart — the side NOT to move has the opposition.

book.author: Nassim Taleb
book.chapter: Build Systems That Gain From Disorder
book.lesson: Taleb's central idea: the opposite of fragile is not robust (survives shocks unchanged) — it is antifragile (gets stronger from shocks). Your muscles are antifragile — stress them and they grow. Your immune system is antifragile. Most institutions are fragile — they optimise for efficiency and have no slack, so unexpected shocks destroy them. To build antifragility: have optionality (many small bets, not one big one), avoid debt (debt makes you fragile to cash flow shocks), benefit from volatility (career skills that are more valuable in crisis than in calm), and build redundancy (slack is not waste — it's the shock absorber).
book.key_quote: Don't just plan to survive crises. Build a life and career that becomes stronger because of them.
book.action: Identify one area of your life (financial, professional, health) that is fragile — one shock away from breaking. What would make it antifragile?
crux: Three categories: fragile (breaks under stress), robust (resists), antifragile (improves).
The opposite of fragile is not robust. It is antifragile — gaining from disorder.
Absence of evidence of fragility is not evidence of robustness. Turkeys learn this at Thanksgiving.
Via negativa: improvement comes more reliably from removal than addition.
Barbell strategy: extreme safety on most of the exposure, extreme risk on a small slice. Never the middle.
Optionality lets you gain from uncertainty without needing to forecast it.
Hormesis: small doses of stress strengthen. Zero stress atrophies.
Naive intervention causes iatrogenic harm — the cure does the damage. Doing nothing is often correct.
Skin in the game is the only real filter. Ignore forecasts from people who bear no cost for being wrong.
Fragility is measurable and predictable; future events are not. Measure the exposure, not the odds.
Time is the best test of durability. The Lindy effect: what has survived long tends to keep surviving.
Redundancy looks inefficient and is actually insurance. Nature runs two kidneys.
Small and decentralised is antifragile; large and centralised is fragile.
Touristification — removing all volatility — makes systems and people brittle.
learnings: Optimise for surviving the worst case, not for the expected case.
Removing the bad reliably beats adding the good.
Anyone forecasting without downside exposure should be discounted to zero.
Efficiency and fragility are usually the same thing wearing different clothes.
examples: Restaurants are individually fragile and the restaurant sector is antifragile — constant failure improves the survivors.
The 2008 banking system was optimised for efficiency, held minimal buffers, and broke. Small distributed lenders did not.
Taleb's barbell in practice: 90% in treasuries, 10% in far out-of-the-money options. Capped loss, uncapped gain.
adapt: Barbell the income: stable FP&A salary as the safe leg, Codex and trading as the small convex leg. No middle-risk bets.
Multiple income paths beat one optimised one. Meta restriction proved single-channel dependence is fragile.
Via negativa on the product: deleting /fno, /options, /portfolio improved TradeFlow. Removal was the upgrade.
Redundancy on the bots: Railway shut down and took the command handler with it. One host is one point of failure.

interview_tech.q: How do you evaluate a capex request for store refurbishment versus a new store?
interview_tech.a: Both need incremental cash flow, but the counterfactual differs. For a new store, the baseline is zero. For a refurbishment, the baseline is the store's declining trajectory without investment — so the benefit is the uplift over that decline, not over today. People systematically overstate refurbishment returns by comparing post-refit sales to pre-refit sales, which double-counts the natural trend and any category resets. Ask for the do-nothing case in writing.

interview_tech.q: What is the one number you would put on a retail CEO's daily dashboard?
interview_tech.a: Like-for-like sales versus plan, with gross margin rate alongside it. One without the other is dangerous — sales up on margin collapse is a discount habit forming, and margin up on sales collapse is a range problem. If forced to a single figure, gross profit versus plan, because it moves only when something real happens. Everything else — footfall, conversion, basket, density — is diagnostic detail you reach for once that number moves.

interview_soft.q: The board pushes back hard on your numbers in front of everyone. What do you do?
interview_soft.a: Do not defend and do not fold. Separate the challenge into fact and judgement. If they have spotted a factual error, concede immediately and precisely — 'you are right, that is the restated base, I will recirculate by Thursday.' Credibility survives errors; it does not survive defensiveness. If it is a judgement call, state your assumption, the sensitivity, and offer the alternative case. Never argue methodology in the room; take it offline with the one director who raised it.

interview_soft.q: An employee asks you to approve an expense that is within policy but clearly wrong. What now?
interview_soft.a: They are testing whether you hide behind rules. Policy is a floor, not a ceiling. Approve or reject on the substance, explain the reasoning to the person directly, and then fix the policy so the next person is not in the same position. If it involves a senior person, the answer does not change — that is precisely when it counts. Say plainly that you would escalate to the audit committee if pressured to approve something you believe is wrong.
interview_soft.who: Any group with a code of conduct

cfo_field.q: Explain a variance in one sentence or you do not understand it yet.
cfo_field.a: 'Margin is down 180bps: 120 from promotional depth in electronics, 40 from freight, 20 mix.' That is a CFO answer. A table of forty lines is a controller answer. The discipline is to decompose until the drivers are additive and then name the largest two. If you cannot make the bridge add up, you have a data problem, not a communication problem.

cfo_field.q: Working capital is where a retail CFO is actually judged.
cfo_field.a: EBITDA gets the headline; the cash conversion cycle gets the board's attention. DIO + DSO − DPO. Retail is inventory-heavy and often near-zero DSO, so the fight is DIO against DPO. Cutting DIO from 95 to 80 days on AED 400M COGS releases roughly AED 16.4M of cash — permanently, without selling a single extra unit. That is a bigger number than most cost programmes deliver, and it does not need a headcount conversation.
